notes.meaning: Zechariah looks up and sees a scroll flying through the air. Ancient books were rolled sheets of parchment or leather, and this one was open so its words could be seen. Flying through the sky showed that God's message travels swiftly and cannot be stopped.

The angel asks what Zechariah sees, and the prophet describes a giant scroll thirty feet long and fifteen feet wide. This massive size matched the porch of Solomon's temple, where God's law was publicly read. Its unusual dimensions showed that God had many serious charges written down against wrongdoers.

The angel explains that the scroll is a curse going out over the entire land to remove thieves and those who swear falsely. Stealing harms other people, while taking false oaths abuses God's holy name, breaking both sides of the Ten Commandments. The scroll has writing on both sides to show that no form of disobedience is overlooked.

The Lord declares that this curse will enter the homes of thieves and liars, remaining there until the whole building is ruined down to its stones and wood. God tracks down hidden sins and will not let dishonest people keep what they gained. Wrongdoing eventually destroys the very places where people think they are safest.

The angel steps forward and tells Zechariah to look up once more at something new approaching. The prophet is invited to pay close attention to the next step in God's plan for his people. God often prepares his servants carefully to help them understand how he deals with evil.

Zechariah asks what is coming, and the angel tells him it is a measuring basket going out across the land. The angel adds that the basket represents the full measure of the people's sins. Just as grain is measured out in a basket, God keeps track of sin until it reaches its limit.

A heavy round lid made of lead is lifted from the basket, revealing a woman sitting inside. The lead cover was very heavy, weighing around seventy-five pounds, to ensure that whatever was inside could not escape. The woman symbolizes the sinful nation and the rebellion of the people.

The angel announces that the woman is Wickedness itself, and he shoves her back into the basket and seals it tightly with the lead weight. This action shows that God will not allow wickedness to run loose or corrupt his restored people. Sin is firmly locked down under the weight of God's judgment.

Zechariah looks up and sees two women flying toward him with large wings like storks, carried swiftly by the wind. They lift the heavy basket high into the air between heaven and earth to carry it far away. God uses these swift agents to remove the burden of sin completely from his land.

Zechariah asks the angel where the two winged figures are carrying the basket. He wants to know the final destination of this trapped evil. Believers can be confident that God knows exactly where he is taking history.

The angel replies that they are taking the basket to Babylon to build a permanent house and place it on a pedestal. Babylon was the historic center of idolatry and rebellion against God, making it the proper home for wickedness. By banishing sin back to its original home, God cleanses his own people so they can live in holiness.
